elements.content: Abstract?Large language models often struggle to synthesize information accurately from complex technical papers containing tables, architecture diagrams, and mathematical formulations. We propose Multimodal-RAG, an architecture combining dense vector embeddings, BM25 inverted keyword indices, and structured extraction of figures and tables. Evaluations demonstrate that incorporating multimodal elements improves Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) by 26.4% and citation accuracy by 34.2% over text-only baselines.

elements.content: 1. Introduction & Problem Statement Scientific literature is inherently multimodal: vital findings, performance metrics, and model layouts reside inside tables and figures rather than body paragraphs. Conventional text-only RAG systems discard non-textual data during document ingestion, yielding hallucinated responses when querying numerical metrics or architecture workflows.

elements.content: 4. Stated Limitations & Hardware Bottlenecks The authors explicitly state that extracting vector diagrams and rasterizing complex mathematical equations introduces a 15-20% latency overhead during initial PDF ingestion. Furthermore, vision-language models required for dense diagram captioning require substantial GPU VRAM, presenting deployment hurdles on edge and CPU-only devices.
